question: Your FastAPI service makes database queries inside a for loop and it's slow. How do you fix it?
title: Fixing the Async N+1 Query Problem
direct_answer: This is the N+1 query problem in async context. Instead of awaiting individual queries in a loop (N+1 round trips), batch the queries: collect all IDs, make one query with WHERE id IN (...), and map results. In SQLAlchemy async, use selectinload or joinedload for relationship loading. With asyncio, you can also run independent queries concurrently with asyncio.gather() — N round trips but parallel instead of serial.
interviewer_intent: Tests whether the candidate can apply database optimization patterns in an async Python context — a common real-world performance problem.

sections.title: N+1 in async context
sections.content:
The N+1 problem: you have a list of 100 user IDs and you query the database once per ID — 1 initial query + 100 individual queries = 101 round trips. Even with async, each round trip takes network latency. 101 sequential awaits × 5ms latency = 505ms. That's slow even though you're using async.

Three solutions depending on context:

1. Batch query: SELECT * FROM users WHERE id IN (1,2,3,...,100). One round trip, O(1) latency. Use when you need all records and the ORM supports it.

2. asyncio.gather(): run all N queries concurrently instead of sequentially. N round trips but parallel — total time ≈ one round trip's latency. Better than sequential awaiting but worse than a single batch query. Use when queries can't be batched (different tables, complex conditions).

3. ORM relationship loading: SQLAlchemy's selectinload or joinedload prefetches related objects in one or two queries. The opposite of the lazy-load anti-pattern that creates N+1.

sections.title: N+1 diagnosis and fixes
sections.content:
from sqlalchemy.ext.asyncio import AsyncSession
from sqlalchemy import select
from sqlalchemy.orm import selectinload
import asyncio

# Problem: N+1 queries — one await per user
async def get_users_slow(user_ids: list[int], db: AsyncSession) -> list:
    users = []
    for uid in user_ids:              # 100 iterations
        result = await db.get(User, uid)  # 100 round trips!
        users.append(result)
    return users

# Fix 1: batch query — one round trip
async def get_users_batch(user_ids: list[int], db: AsyncSession) -> list:
    result = await db.execute(
        select(User).where(User.id.in_(user_ids))
    )
    return result.scalars().all()   # 1 query

# Fix 2: concurrent queries with gather — N parallel round trips
async def get_users_concurrent(user_ids: list[int], db: AsyncSession) -> list:
    return await asyncio.gather(
        *(db.get(User, uid) for uid in user_ids)
    )   # All fire simultaneously, not sequentially

# Fix 3: SQLAlchemy eager loading for relationships
# Problem: accessing user.orders triggers per-user query
async def get_users_with_orders_slow(db: AsyncSession) -> list:
    users = await db.execute(select(User))
    for user in users.scalars():
        _ = user.orders   # N lazy loads!

# Fix: selectinload fetches relationships in one additional query
async def get_users_with_orders_fast(db: AsyncSession) -> list:
    result = await db.execute(
        select(User).options(selectinload(User.orders))  # 2 queries total
    )
    return result.scalars().all()

# Profiling: log slow queries
import logging
logging.getLogger('sqlalchemy.engine').setLevel(logging.INFO)  # see all queries

sections.title: N+1 fix strategy
items: Await in a loop = serial queries — count your round trips
Batch: WHERE id IN (...) — one round trip for all records
gather() — parallel queries when batching isn't possible
selectinload / joinedload — ORM relationship eager loading
Enable SQL query logging to spot N+1 in development

seo.metaDescription: Fix the async N+1 problem in Python: batch queries with IN clause, parallel execution with asyncio.gather, and SQLAlchemy selectinload for relationships.

speakable_v2.hook: Async doesn't fix N+1 — it just makes the 100 sequential queries slightly faster. You still need to batch them.

beats.content: If you see an await inside a for loop over a collection, ask: can these queries be batched? Sequential awaits are still sequential round trips — each one waits for the previous before starting.
The first fix: WHERE id IN (all_ids_at_once). One query, one round trip, regardless of collection size. SQLAlchemy's .in_() makes this a one-liner.
If batching isn't possible — different tables, complex per-item logic — use asyncio.gather(). All queries fire concurrently. Total time is roughly the latency of one query, not N queries.

speakable_v2.cap: Enable SQL query logging in development. If you see 50 nearly-identical queries for one endpoint, you've found N+1.
speakable_v2.followup_handoff: Follow up with connection pool exhaustion when gather fires hundreds of concurrent queries, or SQLAlchemy's async session patterns.
